title: Rav Sama bar Rakta
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In [Kiddushin 9a](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.9a.4) he disagrees with Ravina and swears by the king’s crown. Hyman reports that in [Bava Metzia 10b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.10b.14) he spoke before Ravina in the name of Rabbi Chiyya son of Rav Avya, citing the readings of the Rosh, the Ran and Dikdukei Soferim.[^4]

In the notice cited as ד״ר 14:1, Hyman gives the Radal’s proposed reading: Sama bar Rakta said it in the name of Resh Lakish. The corresponding [Bamidbar Rabbah 14:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Bamidbar_Rabbah.14.1) has Suma bar Katva citing Resh Lakish.

notes.text: The supplied Devarim Rabbah 14:1 reference has not been established as a matching location. A possible parallel is not substituted as proof of that locator. The source question in p002 remains held.

The earlier draft noted a possible Bamidbar Rabbah parallel. A fresh check now finds סומה בר כתבה בשם רבי שמעון בן לקיש in Midrash Rabbah -- TE, Bamidbar Rabbah 14:1. That is a corresponding source for the Katva / Resh Lakish report; it does not verify Devarim Rabbah 14:1, establish the intended expansion of supplied ד״ר, or independently attest the Radal’s proposed Rakta reading.

The printed entry (vol. III, p. 966) uses ד״ר. Hyman’s entry on Suma bar Katva (p. 959) explicitly cites Bamidbar Rabbah 14:1, as does his discussion on p. 1202. The consulted Bamidbar Rabbah has Suma bar Katva in Resh Lakish’s name in the passage about Elijah of Gilead. The consulted transcription of Radal’s note 12 proposes Sama bar Rakta in Resh Lakish’s name. For Bava Metzia 10b, the consulted Rosh (1:30) has Rav Samma bar Rakta speaking before Ravina in Rav Avya’s name, while the commentary on the consulted Rif page (5b) includes Rav Chiyya son of Rav Avya. Hyman’s specific Ran and Dikdukei Soferim readings remain attributed to him.

The [consulted Rosh](https://www.sefaria.org/Rosh_on_Bava_Metzia.1.30.1) names Rav Sama bar Rakta speaking before Ravina in Rav Avya’s name. The Bava Metzia text itself gives only Rav Sama. The [Seder HaDorot entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2810&lang=en) also cites the Rosh. In the Kiddushin passage, the roles are reversed from Heilprin’s account: Ravina rules that she is betrothed, and Rav Sama rules that she is not. The [Radal’s twelfth note](https://or-breslev.co.il/library/חידושי-הרדל-על-במדבר-רבה/פרק-יד/) expressly proposes Rakta for the midrashic name.
